newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe up, Q3 not as bad as feared.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe up, Q3 not as bad as feared.

text.p: Shares of CompuServe Corp were up after the online service reported a third quarter loss that was a bit narrower than some analysts had expected, easing fears that its financials were deteriorating.
CompuServe Chief Executive Officer Robert Massey resigned abruptly on Monday, raising fears on Wall Street that his departure meant bad news in the earnings report.
The Columbus, Ohio-based company, the second-largest U.S. online service, reported a fiscal third quarter loss of $14.2 million, or $0.15 a share.
The First Call consensus estimate was a loss of $0.16 a share.

"They beat my numbers by two cents," said Lisa Thompson, a Prudential Securities analyst. "Revenues were a little bit light, mostly because of CSi (the core online service)...But I'm encouraged by the fact that they are the only ones left without a flat-rate service."
CompuServe exited its flat-rate service, called Wow!, in November. As a result, its CSi subscriber count fell in the third quarter, ended Janury 31, by 150,000.
The company said its exit from Wow!, a service designed mainly for consumers and families, was responsible for 102,000 of the subscriber losses.
Thompson applauded the decision on Wow!. "As a result, they can actually pay content (providers) and have things that others don't have," she said.

Thompson said she is encouraged by the company's strategy to aim its core online service at professional and business users and technical enthusiasts, targeting these users with specific "vertical market" content.
Abhishek Gami, a Nesbitt Burns Securities analyst, said that due to its exit from Wow!, CompuServe spent less on marketing.

"That's why subscriber growth is falling and that's why the stock is up," Gami said. "They are trying to move to a model that is profitable for them. They don't want to compete head to head with MSN (the Microsoft Network) and AOL (America Online). It's a slower growth but more profitable business."
